title: Remote runner inside a TermAl session cannot register runs from an independent TermAl clone (HTTP 400 run directory outside project)
outcome: A runner session on a remote host can run the standard launcher in an approved independent TermAl clone and get a tracked registration, or a clearly documented supported binding, instead of a definitive 400 refusal.
acceptance: C1. A standard-launcher run in an approved independent clone registers durably on its origin host through the existing native session/project/workdir binding and host-owned launch/request correlation. Canonical clone/worktree/run identity and immutable request ownership are checked by the existing registration owner; an arbitrary caller path, wrong project/session, redirected directory or conflicting request is refused before a stage. Existing local registration behavior remains unchanged.

C2. Central can durably wait on an explicitly host-qualified remote native run reference in the caller's project, before terminal completion, through its existing wait owner and authenticated native completion path. The wait pins origin host, native runner/run and original request/project association when available, remains pending while authoritative facts are missing, and does not require a local indexed directory, a preissued job binding, a new registration channel or a fabricated local run. Equal bare run ids on different hosts and foreign projects never alias.

C3. Remote wait settlement consumes the existing origin-host native launcher/process and settlement owner's retained completion correlated with the actual run and original request, preserving native verdict, terminal flag, exit/reason and execution time. Mail prose, caller fields, raw results, a full label or stage count alone cannot supply a success. Missing/Unknown delivery stays nonterminal; genuine failed/interrupted terminals stay failures; conflicting authoritative terminals are visible conflicts. Input qualification and verification-versus-landing use remain solely the final K3 contract, with no new fingerprint, sighting, capture or results-hash condition added by this item.

C4. Registration and remote wait observation grant no verification credit and create no local RegisteredHostRun, producer, grant, turn or source sighting. Until the supported K3/Engram remote_verification_record_v1 capability and genuine current destination association are available, remote runs remain observable but explicitly uncredited using the shared contract's existing reason/detail vocabulary. Qualification and credit association stay with K3 and the Engram-owned admission contract; this item does not implement a second credit path.

C5. Existing bounded authenticated completion recovery and durable wait recovery handle missed, duplicate, late and reordered delivery and restart/reconnect without a duplicate test launch, new model/import turn or new transport. Each wait settles at most once; origin run facts remain separately reusable under K3's valid destination-association checks, and a delivery Unknown cannot occupy an immutable terminal or erase an earlier genuine failure. Existing federation authority/refusal checks remain applicable.

C6. Meaningful tests exercise the actual origin registration and Central wait consumers using real or provenance-preserved producer wire, covering the approved independent-clone path, wrong host/project/request/locator, pending-to-terminal recovery, duplicate/reordered delivery, terminal conflict and restart. Existing local registration/waits remain green; docs describe the supported binding and END-mail fallback; the exact final input has a passing FULL and independent review pair with no outstanding Medium+. Ordinary remote witnesses use only coordinator-authorized slots, with no new manual proof campaign.
